patches.why: CR16CreepyBioCS::UpdateMT worker (0x140a8f200): after a cured creep element's cure timer (+0x23c, set to 3.0 by the cure gun) runs out, `je` falls through to call CureElement(cs,h,cured=0) at 0x140a8f582, which uncures it and it regrows. je->jmp always skips that uncure; the timer still runs down so visuals behave normally.

CR16CreepCystCS state 9 update (0x140a59850, the cured/deflated cyst state): when the cyst is cured (flags&0x60) it ran a regrow timer (+0x24) then SetCystCured(..,0) and moved to state 10 (grow back). Jump straight to the function's `return -1` (stay in state) so a cured cyst never regrows. Uncured (naturally exploded) cysts take the untouched path above and still regrow.

evidence: Creep: CR16SetCreepCuredNode (0x140d6b3e0) -> 0x1409e4cf0 (cure in sphere) -> 0x140a69340 CureElement(cs,handle,cured,?,duration=3.0): sets elem(+0x1c) bit7 and +0x23c=duration. UpdateMT (string 'CR16CreepyBioCS::UpdateMT' 0x140a7dc19) dispatches worker 0x140a8f200 which counts +0x23c down and calls CureElement(...,cured=0) on expiry (0x140a8f582). Cyst: CS registered as symbol R16CreepCyst + update 0x140a7b7c0 + 'CR16CreepCystCS' (0x1408ff3ae..3f0); 14-state machine with handler tables at CS+0xb8/+0x128/+0x198/+0x208 filled at 0x140a299bd; state 9 update calls SetCystCured 0x140a69130(cs,idx,0,0) after timer +0x24 (set to 3.0 by SetCystCured when def+0x50), then returns state 10 (grow anim, +0x54 0->1 at 1/3.33s). NOT verified in game. Static creep (static_creep_logic 'stunned' state, script-side) was not patched: it is a stun, not a cure.
risk: Live-safe (pure branch flips, no state written). Scripted story beats that uncure creep/cysts via other callers (0x140a10ebc, 0x140d59601, CR16ForceCystStateNode) still work. A cyst kept in state 9 forever stays deflated; if a puzzle needed it to regrow (none known) it would softlock -> keep it a toggle. Nothing written to saves by the patch itself, but cured state may be saved as-is. Applied at game launch only: some patches are longer than one atomic 8-byte write, so changing them while the game runs could let a thread execute a half-written instruction.
